newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka town mourns dead MP after riots.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka town mourns dead MP after riots.

text.p: Thousands of people, led by supporters of Sri Lanka's ruling coalition, gathered in this southern gem mining town on Thursday to mourn a government lawmaker who was gunned down earlier this week.

In the wake of two days of rioting, armed policemen and soldiers stood guard over burned out buildings, still smouldering after angry mobs set them on fire after the killing of Nalanda Ellawala, a member of parliament from Ratnapura.

Ellawala, 29, an MP from the ruling People's Alliance, was gunned down in a town near Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) south of Colombo on Tuesday during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and rivals from the main opposition United National Party (UNP).

Police on Thursday issued a nationwide bulletin saying they were looking for UNP member of parliament Susantha Punchinilame and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, a former UNP mayor of Ratnapura, as suspects in the killing.
A statement by the Inspector-General of Police on Thursday said a reward of one million rupees ($17,500) would be paid to anyone providing information leading to the arrest of the pair.
No one was hurt in the riots on Tuesday and Wednesday. But despite the calm that returned to Ratnapura, supporters said more violence could erupt after Ellawala's funeral on Saturday.
"The reaction in the aftermath of the killing was violence and anger," said Vasudeva Nanayakkara, Ellawala's colleague in parliament in the ruling People's Alliance.

"But we're appealing to the people to be calm and urging them to use their emotions to vote against this violent gun culture in the upcoming election," Nanayakkara told Reuters at the dead lawmaker's house.
The killing occurred on the eve of the deadline for filing nominations for the March 21 local polls, the first electoral test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government.
During the riots, police said mobs set fire to scores of shops and buildings, most of them owned by relatives or supporters of the two suspects.
"There have been no incidents of violence today (Thursday) and we are taking all precautions to prevent any more trouble," Ratnapura police chief H.A.D. Sagathapala said.
But party supporters warned of more violence on Saturday.

"We expect about a quarter of a million people to attend the funeral and many of them will be crying mad about this dastardly killing. They can be violent," said Somapala Weerasinghe, another Ellawala supporter.
